audit: Independent Re-Closure Audit - Milestone 2 Critical Repairs (M2_REPAIR_CLOSURE_REFUSED)
ending_commit_note: The ending commit is the single intentional commit 'fix: close paired runner M2 causal index and IPC gaps' created on this branch; its hash is reported in the terminal response and cannot appear inside the object it commits.

findings.closure: Two independent kernel-enforced mechanisms. (1) admissible/paired_runner/capsule_seccomp.py assembles a classic-BPF seccomp program, loaded by bwrap --seccomp immediately before exec, denying socket(AF_UNIX), socketpair(AF_UNIX), mknod, and mknodat with EPERM; SCM_RIGHTS needs no rule because it travels only over an AF_UNIX socket and no AF_UNIX descriptor is ever inherited into the capsule. A mismatched seccomp_data.arch, and on x86-64 any x32 syscall number, kills the process; an architecture with no recorded numbering is a readiness refusal. (2) effects.require_no_workspace_ipc_endpoints refuses to start any capsuled process over a workspace containing a socket, FIFO, or device node, before the durable STARTED record exists.
evidence: WorkspaceIpcBridgeTests: pathname socket, abstract socket, socketpair/SCM_RIGHTS, host FIFO, child-created endpoints, special inode in the initial snapshot, no exported endpoint, ordinary regular-file effects still correct.

SeccompProgramTests: the program is well-formed classic BPF with in-range jumps, a foreign architecture returns SECCOMP_RET_KILL_PROCESS, an unknown architecture raises SeccompUnavailable, and the digest is recorded.
probe_capsule_readiness requires the kernel to demonstrate EPERM for AF_UNIX socket, socketpair, and mkfifo from inside a real capsule.
FilesystemObservation records ipc_endpoint_count and names every endpoint by exact kind; the AFTER_EFFECT observation is the durable proof that nothing was exported.
implementation/M2_WORKSPACE_IPC_ISOLATION_SPEC.md
findings.reproduction: tests/test_admissible_paired_runner_m2_second_repairs.py::WorkspaceIpcBridgeTests::test_the_kernel_really_does_carry_unix_sockets_across_a_network_namespace binds a host pathname AF_UNIX socket, connects to it from a client under `unshare -Urn`, and receives bytes. The audit additionally demonstrated an SCM_RIGHTS transfer of a descriptor for a file outside the namespace. The claim that an unshared network namespace plus an absent evidence path leaves no host capability reachable is withdrawn as false.
findings.title: Pathname Unix sockets bypass mount and network isolation

findings.closure: The observer no longer runs git. admissible/paired_runner/git_observer.py parses HEAD and refs (including packed-refs), the binary index with its trailing SHA-1 verified, and Git objects from loose storage and from packfiles with offset and reference delta resolution, and hashes working-tree files into Git blob identities directly. No denylist is involved because the set of filter names is unbounded. Where the answer would require running a program the observation fails closed with an explicit availability: GIT_CONVERSION_REQUIRED, GIT_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED_LAYOUT, or GIT_METADATA_UNREADABLE. GIT_COMMAND_FAILED, GIT_EXECUTABLE_UNAVAILABLE, and GIT_SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE were removed from the schema, so the record itself testifies that no command is run.
evidence: NonExecutingGitObserverTests: filter.<name>.clean, filter.<name>.process, a required filter, nested .gitattributes, attributes present only in the index/tree, a filter that would mutate the workspace, a filter that would open a Unix socket, a filter that would fork, and core.autocrlf. Every case executes zero repository-controlled programs.

test_the_observation_matches_a_real_client_on_ordinary_repositories differentially compares HEAD, index_dirty, worktree_dirty, and untracked_present against a real git client across clean, worktree-modified, staged, untracked, and missing states.
test_a_packed_repository_is_observed_through_its_packfiles proves object access through .idx/.pack with delta chains after git gc removes every loose object.
MaliciousGitConfigurationTests in tests/test_admissible_paired_runner_m2_repairs.py continue to pass against the non-executing observer.
findings.reproduction: With the shipped GIT_HARDENING_OVERRIDES and GIT_OBSERVATION_ENVIRONMENT applied verbatim, a repository declaring `*.txt filter=evil` in .gitattributes with filter.evil.clean set to a marker script caused `git status --porcelain=v1` to execute that script: the marker log was written. A same-size working-tree modification is what forces the conversion rather than a stat-cache short circuit.
findings.title: Git observation still executes repository-controlled filters

findings.closure: The index is an immutable hash-chained event sequence plus an explicit committed head. durable_sequences() scans every committed name belonging to the run instead of counting until absence, so the position set must be exactly 0..n-1. run-index-anchor is the committed head, the one replaceable object in the store, advanced by atomic rename only after the event it commits is durable. A gap, a surplus position, a duplicate, a reordering, a foreign record, a missing tail relative to the head, an anchor that outruns the chain, an anchor lagging by more than one event, and a missing anchor over a non-empty chain each raise RunIndexBroken.
evidence: The false-positive test is replaced: test_an_omitted_interior_entry_raises_instead_of_truncating requires RunIndexBroken and then restores the entry and requires the complete chain.

test_a_deleted_tail_entry_is_detected_against_the_committed_head, test_a_surplus_entry_beyond_the_head_is_detected, test_a_missing_committed_head_fails_closed, test_a_head_that_outruns_its_events_fails_closed, test_a_forged_head_that_does_not_match_its_event_fails_closed, test_a_cross_run_anchor_is_refused.
Six new fault points cover every event and head publication boundary; each has a literally declared row in implementation/M2_CRASH_MATRIX.json including the run_index_state.
implementation/M2_DURABLE_EVENT_INDEX_SPEC.md, which also states the residual rollback weakness and the external anchor it would require.
findings.reproduction: Publishing entries [0, 1, 2] and deleting entry 1 returned [0] from load_all() with entry 2 still durable and no RunIndexBroken raised. The shipped test test_an_omitted_entry_is_detected asserted that truncated length of 1 as the expected result, so the suite validated the defect. RUN_INDEX_HEAD_KIND was declared and unused.
findings.title: The durable run index accepts omitted entries as a valid shorter run

findings.closure: Every transition is indexed as it happens. The PROPOSAL_PUBLISHED event is durable before the decision is validated and long before the effect boundary, so no effect can exist outside the run's causal order. DECISION_PUBLISHED, RESERVATION_PUBLISHED, EFFECT_STARTED, TERMINAL_RECEIPT_PUBLISHED, and RECONCILIATION_PUBLISHED follow their objects; DECISION_REFUSED, EFFECT_REFUSED_BEFORE_START, and EFFECT_AMBIGUOUS are terminal refusal events. effects.recover_run_index derives the missing events from durable bytes and appends only those; it writes no proposal, reservation, lifecycle record, receipt, or reconciliation, and RunIndexRecovery.replayed_any_effect is structurally false.
evidence: test_a_completed_effect_whose_index_event_was_lost_is_recovered removes the closing event, rewinds the head, recovers, and asserts the workspace bytes are unchanged and the effect was not re-executed.
test_the_proposal_is_indexed_before_any_effect_is_possible and test_every_transition_of_every_proposal_is_indexed.
Every HEAD_UPDATE_PENDING crash row is recovered in tests/test_admissible_paired_runner_m2_crash.py, with the effect invocation count and workspace state re-asserted afterwards.
test_a_pending_committed_head_blocks_an_append_until_it_is_recovered.
findings.reproduction: The single end-of-proposal summary was appended after the typed final reconciliation. A process death in that window left a real effect, a verified final reconciliation, and a durable ledger entry with no index entry at all, so the run's authoritative order silently omitted a completed effect.
findings.title: A fully reconciled effect can crash before it is indexed

findings.closure: The proposal_ids parameter is gone. The ordered proposal set is derived from the durable run index, which is itself chain-verified against its committed head first. Every indexed proposal's whole typed chain is reconciled; an effect-bearing proposal must have a ledger entry whose record and receipt fingerprints the index already recorded; a refused proposal must have no ledger entry and that absence is checked; a ledger entry the index never recorded is surplus and fails closed. SharedEffectSubstrate.preflight rebuilds the in-memory ledger from that derived history before any new proposal is published, and RunEffectLedger.adopt permits extension only. The proposal and effect-receipt ledger fingerprints include the durable index head and the entry count.
evidence: test_verification_takes_no_caller_supplied_history inspects the signature and requires every remaining parameter to be keyword-only.
test_a_restart_reconstructs_the_complete_history_before_a_new_effect runs three proposals, restarts with an empty ledger, runs a fourth, and requires the complete ordered history.

test_no_historical_proposal_can_be_omitted, test_a_ledger_entry_the_index_never_recorded_is_surplus, test_a_refusal_carries_no_ledger_entry_and_that_absence_is_checked, test_an_in_memory_ledger_that_contradicts_the_durable_history_refuses, test_the_ledger_fingerprints_bind_the_complete_history.
findings.reproduction: RunEffectLedger.verify(store, run_id, proposal_ids, ...) took the history to check from its caller. A restarted process with an empty in-memory ledger could pass an empty or partial tuple and receive a ledger that verified perfectly while omitting every effect the run had already performed.
findings.title: Effect-ledger verification permits caller-selected historical omission

findings.closure: admissible/paired_runner/capsule_identity.py derives a typed CapsuleRuntimeManifest binding the launcher's canonical path, SHA-256, device, inode, owner, mode, size, and version; the interpreter's path, SHA-256, device, inode, size, mode, and owner; the in-capsule init's SHA-256 and size; the seccomp program's SHA-256, architecture, and instruction count; a source identity over every module of the package; the declared toolchain roots with their inode identities; and the namespace, mount, and containment contract. Each file is hashed through one descriptor so the stat and the read describe the same object, and a group- or world-writable input, or one owned by neither root nor this user, is refused outright. The manifest is rechecked in preflight, before the proposal is durable, including re-resolving the launcher through PATH so a shadowing entry is caught even when the recorded absolute path still holds the original bytes.
evidence: CapsuleRuntimeIdentityTests: a replaced launcher, a replaced interpreter, a replaced init, a moved inode, a changed package source identity, a PATH substitution with the recorded bytes intact, and a group-writable input are each refused.
test_a_substituted_capsule_refuses_before_the_proposal_is_durable proves the refusal is pre-proposal: the proposal object is ABSENT afterwards.
The manifest is published durably per run and its fingerprint is bound by every EFFECT_STARTED index event and by the capsule descriptor.
findings.reproduction: The capsule descriptor bound the mechanism name and the path shutil.which resolved, and nothing about the bytes behind that name. A replaced bwrap, a substituted interpreter, an edited in-capsule init, or a PATH entry shadowing the launcher would each have produced identical evidence for a different boundary.
findings.title: Capsule mechanism and helper identities are not bound to their bytes

findings.closure: Per-command bounds are applied by the in-capsule init in the forked child immediately before execv, which is the only point that bounds the command without also bounding the supervisor: processes, address space, CPU seconds derived from the request's own timeout, open files, file size, and a prohibited core dump, each set with soft and hard equal except RLIMIT_CPU whose hard limit is one second later so the SIGXCPU-then-SIGKILL escalation is observable. A per-effect cgroup v2 subtree is added on top when the host delegates one, bounding the whole process domain in aggregate. The child reads the limits back with getrlimit and reports them through the pre-exec pipe, so ResourceObservation records enforcement rather than intent. A bound that cannot be set is fatal to the child.
evidence: ResourceContainmentTests: fork bomb, memory allocation, descriptor exhaustion, large-file write, timeout with namespace-wide escalation, effective bounds recorded durably, and an unrelated host process untouched.

probe_capsule_readiness runs the real init with the real bounds argument and requires the kernel to stop a fork loop with EAGAIN, a 1 GiB allocation with MemoryError, and a descriptor loop with EMFILE; any failure is SandboxUnavailable before any proposal.

probe_cgroup_delegation physically creates and removes a subtree rather than inferring delegation from the presence of /sys/fs/cgroup; on the qualification host it reports unavailable and the recorded mechanism is RLIMIT.
implementation/M2_RESOURCE_CONTAINMENT_SPEC.md
findings.reproduction: The capsule applied no CPU, memory, process-count, file-size, or descriptor limit and no core-dump prohibition. A PID namespace is a naming boundary, not a quota, so a fork bomb or an allocator reaches the host before the wall-clock timeout is what stops it.
findings.title: The untrusted process domain has no resource containment

findings.closure: The descriptor is fstat-ed again after the last byte is read and the two identities are compared over device, inode, size, mtime_ns, ctime_ns, and link count. A moved identity yields the explicit error entry_changed_while_it_was_being_hashed, which marks the observation INCOMPLETE_OBSERVATION_ERROR and OBSERVED_BEST_EFFORT, so it can never serve as a final repository fingerprint.
evidence: ObservationRaceTests::test_a_same_size_mutation_during_hashing_is_detected performs a concurrent same-size rewrite during the hash and requires the detection and the incomplete classification.
test_the_stable_identity_covers_every_field_a_rewrite_can_move covers the audited same-size case directly.
test_a_quiet_file_still_hashes_completely proves the check does not make ordinary observations incomplete.
findings.reproduction: _hash_regular_file fstat-ed before reading and never after, so a concurrent writer could change the file during the read and the resulting digest covered a mixture of two versions that never existed together on disk, reported as a complete observation.
findings.title: Filesystem observations do not detect a file changing during hashing

findings.closure: Replaced with an exact comparison against SUPPORTED_SPECIFICATION_SCHEMA_VERSION, the constant this substrate implements, and moved to the head of preflight so an unsupported specification is refused before anything else is inspected on the strength of it.
evidence: SchemaPreflightTests::test_the_check_is_against_the_supported_version asserts the tautology is gone from the source and the constant is used.
SchemaPreflightTests::test_an_unsupported_specification_schema_is_refused requires ConfigurationRefused with code SCHEMA_VERSION_MISMATCH.
findings.reproduction: preflight contained `if specification.schema_version != specification.schema_version:`, which can never be true.
findings.title: A schema preflight check is tautological

known_limitations: Deleting the newest run-index event AND rewinding the committed head to a still-valid earlier head is a rollback no purely local record can detect. DurableRunIndex.head_anchor() is the exact value an external anti-rollback anchor would pin; Milestone 2 implements no such anchor.

The workspace remains a bidirectionally shared host directory by contract. Admission proves no IPC endpoint exists when a capsuled process starts and the seccomp boundary proves the command cannot create one, but a host process that creates a FIFO in the workspace mid-execution is outside both mechanisms.
The capsule denies every AF_UNIX socket and every mknod. A command needing local socket IPC or a FIFO fails with EPERM. This is the documented contract of the capsule, not a defect.

The non-executing Git observer counts every working-tree path the index does not track as untracked; ignore rules are deliberately not evaluated, so that count is a superset of a git client's. The exact semantics are recorded in the observation's untracked_semantics field.

A repository declaring any content conversion (a filter, text, eol, ident, or working-tree-encoding attribute, a [filter ...] configuration section, or core.autocrlf) is observed as GIT_CONVERSION_REQUIRED rather than compared, because the working-tree-to-blob mapping would be a repository-defined computation.
Git index version 4 and a .git file layout (linked worktree or submodule) are refused as GIT_REPOSITORY_UNSUPPORTED_LAYOUT rather than parsed.

The qualification host delegates no writable cgroup v2 subtree, so the containment mechanism in force is RLIMIT and aggregate process-domain accounting is unavailable. This is recorded in every resource observation rather than assumed away.
RLIMIT_AS bounds address space rather than resident set, and disk space as a whole is not bounded; RLIMIT_FSIZE bounds any single file.
Child CPU and peak RSS remain OBSERVED_BEST_EFFORT because getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) aggregates every reaped child of the controller. The enforced bounds are OBSERVED; the measurements are not.
The model, executable, and transport identities in the experiment specification remain Milestone 1 placeholders. The capsule runtime manifest binds the capsule's own byte identity only.
Isolation depends on unprivileged user namespaces and seccomp filter loading being available on the host. Where they are not, readiness refuses before any effect rather than degrading.

Filesystem observation streams file bytes, so observation cost is proportional to workspace size; a workspace exceeding the entry or byte limit yields an explicit incomplete observation that cannot serve as a final repository fingerprint.
The run index is single-session and provider-free by construction; multi-session continuation is deliberately absent and is not implied by it.
No installed-path, production-root, or owner-authority behaviour is exercised or claimed.
modification_rationale: The Milestone 2 critical-repair commit did not pass independent re-closure. Findings M2-B12 through M2-B16 and M2-M17 through M2-M20 are closed here and only here. Milestone 3 was not begun.

withdrawn_claims.claim: An unshared network namespace plus an absent evidence path means no host capability is reachable from the capsule.
withdrawn_claims.reason: A pathname AF_UNIX socket is a filesystem object that crosses an unshared network namespace and can transfer an open file descriptor with SCM_RIGHTS; a FIFO in the writable workspace is the same bridge. Reproduced physically before repair.
withdrawn_claims.replaced_by: The command sees no host-backed IPC endpoint and cannot create an IPC endpoint visible to a host process during execution, enforced by a seccomp syscall boundary and by workspace admission.

withdrawn_claims.claim: Command-line -c overrides neutralise every repository-controlled setting through which Git can execute a program.
withdrawn_claims.reason: A repository selects an arbitrary filter driver by name through .gitattributes and defines it in its own configuration; the set of names is unbounded, so no denylist closes it. Reproduced with the shipped override list.
withdrawn_claims.replaced_by: A non-executing observer that parses refs, the index, and object storage directly and fails closed where the answer would require running a program.

withdrawn_claims.claim: The durable run index detects an omitted entry.
withdrawn_claims.reason: load_all() stopped at the first absent object and returned a shorter chain that verified; the shipped test asserted that truncated length as success.
withdrawn_claims.replaced_by: A full scan of every durable name belonging to the run, plus an explicit committed head with named crash states.
